I hit the tool ceiling mid-documentation, so the archive isn't packaged yet. Here's exactly where things stand — all the code for Slice 48 is written and verified; what remains is finishing the documentation edits and tarring it up.

The blocking failure is fixed
docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md:1335 reproduced the forbidden platform-state claim verbatim while explaining why archived history is exempt from that very rule. I've rewritten the clause to describe the sentence instead of quoting it, and verified the gate's subject is now clean — zero matches for any of the ten forbidden phrasings across the spec.

The repair is recorded as F-98, and the lesson is the part worth keeping: a paragraph explaining why a forbidden string is exempt somewhere is the paragraph most likely to contain that string. A gate over authored text gets tripped by its own documentation before it gets tripped by a defect. Adding the spec to RECORD_FILES was rejected — that would put 449 KiB of normative prose outside the rule, which is the argument the gate's own comment makes against hygiene exemptions.

The menu verb — Stage 3b, written and structurally verified
ResequenceMenuItemsAsync mirrors the section verb one register down, with three decisions that weren't settled by Slice 47's design:

The heading is a parameter, not inferred from the list. A position is a position within a section, so sending the whole menu would ask the write to renumber the puddings because somebody moved a drink.

Three outcomes, not four. An unknown heading returns no rows, so it reaches MenuItemSetChanged through the same permutation comparison every other refusal does. That's deliberate: an unknown heading and a stale item set are one fact from the surface's side — this page is stale, reload it — and a distinction the caller can't act on differently isn't worth returning. There's an explicit integration fact pinning it, because "no rows came back" is also what an empty heading looks like, and the two agreeing should be a decision rather than an accident.

The section row is not locked, and the argument is arithmetic. A concurrent create or refile appends at MAX(display_order) + 1 computed from the very positions the resequence holds: n rows with maximum m give m ≥ n-1, so the arrival lands at m+1 ≥ n — strictly after every position the resequence can assign, which is exactly the append those verbs promise. So the interleaving is correct with no lock, and taking none means this verb adds no new lock ordering to reason about. It takes item locks and nothing else, where a refile takes item-then-section; a section lock here would invert that nesting and make the deadlock question live for the first time.

Files changed: MenuAdministration.cs (enum, locking SQL, interface, implementation, permutation helper), MenuWorkflow.cs (interface + one conditional publish), AdministrationMenu.razor (Up/Down per item row, handler, two end-of-list helpers, form-name helper, three flash sentences, header comment, lede), plus MenuWiringTests.cs (fake learns the verb, two new facts) and a new MenuItemResequenceTests.cs (eight assertions).

Verification run: string-aware brace balance passed on all five C# files; the Razor tag-tree walk passed on the edited page; no CS4007 or CS1620 hazards; every constructor and helper signature I call was confirmed against the tree.

Two things resolved without an edit
F-93's obligation was already discharged. .record-actions button has been in the barrier's selector since it was written — and matched nothing until this slice. The item rows are the first submit controls to render in an actions cell. No edit was needed, and that's the finding rather than the relief: a selector matching nothing is indistinguishable from one matching everything it should. What makes it safe is that .menu-group-actions button was already asserting the same claim elsewhere on this page. I've recorded that in the barrier's own comment.

MinimumControlsMeasured = 14 is a floor, so more controls can only help it. Only MinimumCountedClasses moves — 23 → 24, for the new §16.4 paragraph.

Also fixed in passing
The xUnit2031 warning at MenuSectionResequenceTests.cs:249 — switched to the filtering overload of Assert.Single, with a note that the analyzer is right about the failure message.

Predicted test count
1180 → 1190: eight assertions in MenuItemResequenceTests, two in MenuWiringTests. Per §18, any deviation from 1190 is the first thing to chase.

What's left, and it's all documentation
Appendix A needs the F-98 row and the Stage 3b enhancement row (I was reading the rows after F-97 when I ran out); then the changelog entry for v1.33, the DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md status line and F-98 row, the BUILD_PROGRESS.md Slice 48 entry, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md (strike Stage 3b, record what landed and the three things design didn't settle), and _CHANGES.md. Then the SpecificationVersionTests and TestingSectionContractTests simulations, byte hygiene, and the tar.

The menu verb — Stage 3b, written and structurally verified
ResequenceMenuItemsAsync mirrors the section verb one register down, with three decisions that weren't settled by Slice 47's design:

The heading is a parameter, not inferred from the list. A position is a position within a section, so sending the whole menu would ask the write to renumber the puddings because somebody moved a drink.

Three outcomes, not four. An unknown heading returns no rows, so it reaches MenuItemSetChanged through the same permutation comparison every other refusal does. That's deliberate: an unknown heading and a stale item set are one fact from the surface's side — this page is stale, reload it — and a distinction the caller can't act on differently isn't worth returning. There's an explicit integration fact pinning it, because "no rows came back" is also what an empty heading looks like, and the two agreeing should be a decision rather than an accident.

The section row is not locked, and the argument is arithmetic. A concurrent create or refile appends at MAX(display_order) + 1 computed from the very positions the resequence holds: n rows with maximum m give m ≥ n-1, so the arrival lands at m+1 ≥ n — strictly after every position the resequence can assign, which is exactly the append those verbs promise. So the interleaving is correct with no lock, and taking none means this verb adds no new lock ordering to reason about. It takes item locks and nothing else, where a refile takes item-then-section; a section lock here would invert that nesting and make the deadlock question live for the first time.
